message.content:
It’s hard to pick just one “best” film from 2020 because tastes vary so much, but here are a few titles that received widespread acclaim and are often cited as standout releases of that year:

| Film | Why it stood out |
|------|------------------|
| **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | A sharp, timely courtroom drama written and directed by Aaron Sorkin that earned praise for its ensemble cast, tight pacing, and topical relevance. |
| **“Soul”** | Pixar’s Oscar‑winning animated feature that blends humor, music, and philosophical depth, winning both Best Animated Feature and Best Original Song. |
| **“Tenet”** | Christopher Nolan’s ambitious sci‑fi thriller that pushed the limits of visual storytelling and action choreography, earning a cult following despite mixed reviews. |
| **“Mank”** | David Fincher’s biopic about screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz, lauded for its period detail, strong performances, and sharp dialogue. |
| **“Nomadland”** | Though released in late 2019, it dominated the 2020 awards circuit, winning Best Picture at the Oscars and praised for its quiet, contemplative storytelling. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best” according to critics, many would point to **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** or **“Soul”** as the most celebrated films of 2020. If you prefer a more personal recommendation, let me know your genre preferences and I can narrow it down further!
